title: A Teen Swimmer From Ohio Just Made a Huge Splash — Committing to Texas A&M
summary:
Have you ever dreamed of swimming for a big college team? Owen Gee just made that dream real. He's a high school swimmer from Morrow, Ohio, and he's only in the class of 2028. But he already knows where he's going: Texas A&M University!

Owen swims for the Cincinnati Marlins and St. Xavier High School. At a big summer meet, he swam the 200 butterfly in 2 minutes and 1.18 seconds — that's fast enough to finish 4th in the prelims. He also swam the 100 butterfly in 54.23 seconds and the 100 freestyle in 51.42 seconds.

Back in February, he finished 3rd in the 100 fly at the Ohio state championships. He was also 2nd in the 500 free and helped his relay team win.

"I am honored and thankful to announce my commitment to continue my athletic and academic career at Texas A&M!" Owen wrote.

He thanked his family, his coaches, and his teammates. Then he added the Texas A&M cheer: "Gig 'Em!"

Owen will arrive at Texas A&M in fall 2028. That's still a few years away — but for a swimmer this fast, the future looks bright.
why_it_matters: It shows that training at something year after year — and saying your goal out loud — can open big doors, even while you are still in school.

background_read: Texas A&M University (a big public university in Texas, USA, whose sports teams are called the Aggies) has strong swimming teams, and 'Gig 'Em!' is the school's famous cheer.
In the United States, student athletes often promise to join a college team years before they finish high school — that promise is called a commitment.
High school swimmers usually compete for a club team too, like Owen's Cincinnati Marlins, so they can swim faster and be noticed by college coaches.
